messages.subject: Confidence intervals with loess
parts:
Hi everyone -

It appears that there's a bug in stat_smooth: when you use a loess fit, it always gives a 68% confidence interval, no matter what value you specify for 'level'. 

https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/issues/298

For example, these two graphs will give the exact same output:
ggplot(cars, aes(x=speed, y=dist)) + geom_point() + stat_smooth(level=.99)
ggplot(cars, aes(x=speed, y=dist)) + geom_point() + stat_smooth(level=.2)


I have a potential solution using the t-distribution to calculate confidence intervals from the standard error. Hadley asked me to check with the list to see if anyone knows whether confidence intervals should be calculated from the t distribution or z distribution.

Any experts want to weigh in?

Thanks,
-Winston

messages.author: 065110cca96a6373
messages.subject: Re: Confidence intervals with loess
parts:
You might take a look at Cleveland & Devlin 1988.  The discuss lowess and also using the trace of the L matrix to approximate the degrees of freedom.  This also reminds me of what is done with splines for which you might poke around elements of statistical learning by Hastie Tibshirani and Friedman.

Cheers,

Josh
